column3: NASB supplies “reached”; “at the extreme south” renders “from the end of the south.”
“the ascent of Akrabbim” transliterates “the ascent of scorpions.”
“the brook of Egypt” renders “the wadi of Egypt”; “the border ended at the sea” renders “the extremities of the border were toward the sea.”
“the mouth of the Jordan” renders “the end of the Jordan.”
NASB puts “that is, Jerusalem” in parentheses.
NASB puts “that is, Kiriath-jearim” in parentheses.
“the border ended at the sea” renders “the extremities of the border were toward the sea.”
“he gave” renders the impersonal “someone gave”; “the command” renders “the mouth,” and NASB supplies “Arba being.”
NASB supplies “to him”; “persuaded” renders “incited,” and “What do you want?” renders “What is to you?”
